clue.text: See 16
Bill runs before I sup what's found in coaltar

blocks.note: AC is short for account, a bill
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs
taken as written
to sup is to eat an evening meal

explanation.surface: Someone settles the bill before eating, in a clue that drifts oddly into industrial chemistry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' simply places the bill and runs ahead of the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Acridine is a nitrogen-containing chemical compound originally isolated from the heavy fraction of coal tar.

clue.text: Great way to butt in to pious pep talk

indicators.note: something that butts in pushes its way into the middle of whatever follows

blocks.note: pious means devout
the M1, Britain's first long motorway, with its 1 written as I

explanation.surface: A preacher barges in on a motivational talk to make it devout.
explanation.walkthrough: The road splits the pious word after its first two letters. The M1 is the motorway from London to Yorkshire; crosswords often write it MI.
explanation.definitionFit: A homily is a sermon or a moralising lecture, which is close to an earnest pep talk given to improve behaviour.

clue.text: The widow gave one pronounced strength

indicators.note: pronounced tells us to go by how a word is said, not spelt

blocks.note: might is power or strength

explanation.surface: A biblical widow made a gift with obvious force of character.
explanation.walkthrough: In Mark's gospel a poor widow gives two mites, tiny coins, and is praised above the rich givers.
explanation.definitionFit: The widow's mite is the small coin she put in the temple treasury, so one coin of hers is exactly this.

clue.text: Stir up tons of rolled oats for breakfast

indicators.note: rolled oats are flattened and turned, so the word oats is turned about

blocks.note: to egg on is to urge or stir up
T is the abbreviation for tons
the four letters reordered

explanation.surface: A cook stirs a huge vat of porridge oats for the morning meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rolled oats' reads as porridge, which seems to be the breakfast; it is an anagram signal and its fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A boiled or scrambled egg served on a slice of toast is a classic morning meal, an example of breakfast.

clue.text: Go to wrap a train set for Antonio's friend

indicators.note: set here means arranged, so the letters are put into a new order
a word that wraps another goes around it on both sides

blocks.note: taken as written
the six letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone goes off to gift-wrap a toy train set for a friend's present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'train set' looks like a toy, but set is the anagram signal for the two words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Gratiano is a talkative companion of the merchant Antonio in Shakespeare's The Merchant of Venice.

clue.text: Rigorous in diagnosis of gastric trauma

indicators.note: a diagnosis looks inside the patient, so the answer is found within the next words

blocks.note: letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A doctor is exacting when assessing a stomach injury.
explanation.definitionFit: Strict and rigorous are synonyms, both describing exact, demanding standards applied without leniency.

clue.text: See 16
Blustering Trojan warrior cringes at heart

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its centre, so only its middle letters are kept

blocks.note: Hector was Troy's champion in the Iliad
the central three of its seven letters

explanation.surface: A boastful Trojan hero secretly cowers inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To hector is to bully with loud, swaggering talk, so hectoring behaviour is blustering and intimidating.

clue.text: An unending share of pie reported, for example...

indicators.note: without an ending, the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: a ration is an allotted share

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a smaller helping of pie than usual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pie reported' means pi, said the same way; pi is the ratio of a circle's circumference to its diameter, hence 'for example'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pi is defined as the circumference of a circle divided by its diameter, so it is one instance of a ratio.

clue.text: ... since you, say, and I organised the cooking

indicators.note: say indicates the word you is only spoken, giving its sound
organised means put into a fresh arrangement, so the letters are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written
the letter U is pronounced like you
taken as written

explanation.surface: Continuing the pie conversation: because the two of us arranged things, we did the cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuisine is a style of food preparation, a fancier word for the cooking of a place or kitchen.

clue.text: See 16
One of the Mitfords, single and unknown

blocks.note: a unit is one single thing
algebra uses x, y and z for unknowns

explanation.surface: A gossip notes that one of the famous sisters is unmarried and obscure.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mitfords were six aristocratic English sisters of the 1930s, famous for writing and politics.
explanation.definitionFit: Unity Mitford, a notorious admirer of Hitler, was one of the six celebrated Mitford sisters.

clue.text: In retrospect, heartless Greek character covering motor in Manx race was fascinated

indicators.note: without a heart, the word loses its central letter
covering means wrapping round what follows, so the next part sits inside
looking back in retrospect means reading everything from the end

blocks.note: the fourth letter of the Greek alphabet
a motor is a car
the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race on the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: Someone recalls a Greek spectator at the Isle of Man races who was spellbound by the bikes.
explanation.walkthrough: The Greek letter loses its middle letter and wraps the motor-inside-race piece; the whole string is then read from right to left. The TT is a famous motorcycle race on the Isle of Man.
explanation.definitionFit: To be attracted is to be drawn towards or captivated by something, so fascinated is a close synonym.

clue.text: One's obtained improved defensive organisms

indicators.note: something improved has been reworked, so the letters are remade into a new order

blocks.note: one is I, and the apostrophe s gives S
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone has secured better protection, as if against germs.
explanation.definitionFit: Antibodies are protective proteins made by the immune system; calling them defensive organisms is loose but fair for a crossword.

clue.text: One doesn't care for sprouts after dark?

definitions.text: One doesn't care for sprouts after dark?

blocks.note: surface reading: vegetables such as Brussels sprouts, which nobody looks after at night

blocks.clueFragment: One doesn't care for sprouts after dark?
blocks.note: setter's reading: sprouts are small children, and this place minds them only during working hours

explanation.walkthrough: 'sprouts' suggests a garden or greenhouse; it is slang for youngsters, and the place stops caring for them when it closes in the evening.
explanation.definitionFit: A nursery that takes young children in daytime hours while parents work, returning them home before night.

clue.text: (see also 24,23 across, 8,22 down, 12 across and 1 down) Bush analysis based on theory of judicious statesman: vote for my mother; cut Tom Prior out

annotation.answer: THE VAST MAJORITY OF OUR IMPORTS COME FROM OUTSIDE THE COUNTRY

indicators.note: the closing word says the preceding letters are put out of their order and laid out afresh

blocks.note: taken letter for letter
taken letter for letter
taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A spin doctor sells a candidate's homely policies while quietly dropping an awkward colleague called Tom Prior.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a famous George W. Bush gaffe, spread over seven lights. All 52 letters before the final word are rearranged; 'based on' merely links them to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This rambling remark about trade is one of the best-known Bushisms, so it is literally an analysis offered by President Bush.

clue.text: Gold about to inspire saucy opening

indicators.note: to inspire is literally to breathe in, so the next word is drawn inside

blocks.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
re means concerning or about
pert means cheeky or saucy

explanation.surface: Gold jewellery is meant to give someone a cheeky, daring look.
explanation.walkthrough: The saucy word goes between the A and the U of the gold symbol, with RE after.
explanation.definitionFit: An aperture is a hole or gap, such as the opening in a camera lens that lets light through.

clue.text: Rude Italian woman headed off with books

indicators.note: headed off means losing the head, so the first letter goes

blocks.note: the Italian title for a married woman
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A boorish Italian lady storms off clutching her books.
explanation.walkthrough: Rude here has its older sense of uneducated or unlearned, not impolite.
explanation.definitionFit: Rude can mean primitive or untaught, as in rude peasants, which matches lacking knowledge.

clue.text: Doctor taken by investing two notes on a multiple flutter

indicators.note: investing means clothing or surrounding, so the following pair goes inside
to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are altered in order

blocks.note: taken letter for letter
E is a musical note, taken twice

explanation.surface: A doctor gambles a couple of banknotes on a complicated wager.
explanation.walkthrough: A flutter is British slang for a small bet. A Yankee is a bet on four selections combined into eleven separate wagers.
explanation.definitionFit: A Yankee is a combination wager covering doubles, trebles and an accumulator, so it is a multiple bet.

clue.text: Sancho ordered some chips

indicators.note: ordered means put into an arrangement, so the name's letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the name taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Sancho Panza orders a side of fries at the inn.
explanation.definitionFit: Nachos are tortilla chips served with toppings, so they are a portion of chips.

clue.text: Rear Posh as a believer?

blocks.note: hind means at the back
U means upper class, a British label for posh usage

explanation.surface: A gossip wonders whether Posh Spice is raising her children in a faith.
explanation.walkthrough: Posh Spice of the Spice Girls is the hint the surface wants; U is the old British label for upper-class speech and manners.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hindu is a follower of Hinduism, one particular kind of religious believer, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Occur, maybe, in Yorkshire

blocks.note: first meaning: to take place
second meaning: a northern English dialect word for perhaps

explanation.walkthrough: Yorkshire is a large county in northern England, where people say 'happen' to mean perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Events happen when they occur, and in Yorkshire dialect the same word is used as an adverb meaning perhaps.

clue.text: Like a jewel one time, seized by US agent

indicators.note: seized by means held inside the grip of what comes next

blocks.note: a Fed is an FBI agent
an ace is a one in cards
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A gem once confiscated by an American federal officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A cut gemstone has many flat polished faces called facets, so being faceted is a typical jewel quality.

clue.text: See 16
See 16
Do I not idolise the German girl?

indicators.note: not idolise with these letters means idolise without them, so they are taken away

blocks.note: taken as written, before the two named parts are removed

explanation.surface: A suitor asks whether he fails to adore the German girl.
explanation.walkthrough: From idolise remove DO and one I, as the opening words say, leaving a German first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Ilse is a common German girl's name, a form of Elisabeth, so the definition names an example.

clue.text: See 16
Oriental festival a winner? Not half!

indicators.note: not half means only part survives, so the front half of the word is dropped

blocks.note: the Christian spring festival
taken as written

explanation.surface: Is the spring festival a triumph? Absolutely, says the speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' sounds like British slang for an emphatic yes; here it really removes half of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: An Oriental is a person from the East, and an easterner is equally someone from an eastern region.
